Definition: to rush upon; by implication, to toss (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative)
BiblicalUsage: çâʻar is the word for to rush upon, to toss. It turns up 7 times in the Old Testament, and wherever it lands it keeps that same plain sense. In 2 Kings and Habakkuk you can see it doing exactly what the word says.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe çâʻar matters because God gave us the word for to rush upon, to toss. God did not put this word in Scripture 7 times for us to skip over it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
